cause_quote: The diff added `guard self.streamingTextShape(text) != previousShape else { return }` before `self.markTimelineChanged()`, so new words stopped triggering the scroll handler once the live bubble was visible.
user_saw: With the iOS keyboard open, long replies streamed out of view and could jump or leave a blank space when they finished.
summary: The fix follows the bottom edge as streaming text grows, coordinates the swap to the saved reply, and moves the working indicator below the text.
reasoning: I checked the parent of #168919 and confirmed that every changed stream update advanced the timeline revision, which made the keyboard-open follow path scroll to the bottom. #168919 gated those updates on changes to the bubble's visibility and relied on SwiftUI's size-change anchor for ordinary text growth, which the fix's simulator evidence showed left replies out of view. The working indicator was already above the reply before #168919, so the 42-point finish jump has a separate origin.
